subject: typewriter
pitch: A 1930s typewriter in glossy racing green. Round keys with cream letters on chrome rims in four staggered rows, a semicircle of thin type bars behind them, a chrome carriage return lever, a black platen roller with a sheet of paper half typed, and a small brass maker's badge on the front.

I'm figuring out the joint setup — probably a simple root joint for the static base plus a posable pivot joint for the carriage return lever — and now I'm nailing down exact box coordinates for the body, keeping its bottom resting at y=0, and choosing a glossy racing-green color for the casing.

I'm switching to an extruded side-profile approach for the body: drawing the (z,y) outline of the typewriter's silhouette — sloped keyboard front, lip, and rear deck — then extruding it along x to form the solid side panels.

For the keys themselves, I'm figuring out how to place them along that sloped front deck so they look like they emerge naturally from the incline rather than floating on a flat plane.

Placing keys as cylinders with frames oriented along the slope normal so they rise naturally out of the deck, then layering a chrome rim cylinder plus a cream top for each key to get the vintage two-tone look.

Rather than 36 separate textures, I'm now favoring one shared atlas sheet laid out as a 10×4 grid, where each key's circle geometry gets a remapped UV offset into its own cell -- computing u'/v' per vertex based on column and row position. That way every key references the same single texture but renders its own letter cell.
